passages.title: Driver and Vehicle Standards Agency: Business Plan 2026-27
passages.speaker: The Parliamentary Under-Secretary of State for Transport (Justin Madders)
passages.body: I am pleased to announce the publication of the 2026 to 2027 business plan for the Driver and Vehicle Standards Agency. DVSA’s business plan sets out the key business priorities the agency will deliver, including any significant changes it plans to make to its services, and performance indicators by which its performance will be assessed. passages.body: My Lords, on 15 October, in your Lordships’ House, my noble friend Lady Monckton asked the Minister: “How many of this cohort” of foreign national offenders “who are liable to deportation remain in the United Kingdom due to Article 8 claims and human rights claims?”.—[Official Report, 15/10/26; col. 337.] The Minister, the noble Lord, Lord Lemos, answered that that information was available but not yet in a form to be published. I wonder if the noble Lord could update the House on that.

passages.title: Shabir Ahmed
passages.speaker: Lord Collins of Highbury (Lab)
passages.body: We are pursuing every available option to deport Shabir Ahmed, and, as I say, it would be inappropriate to give a running commentary on those discussions. Since coming to power, this Government have returned nearly 12,000 foreign national offenders between 1 July 2024 and 31 July 2026. That figure includes both enforced and voluntary returns. Compared with the final two years of the previous Government, foreign national offender returns have increased by 41%.
